blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Ombudsman now has direct access to government procurement records, allowing the anti-graft body to speed up its investigation and prosecution work and prevent corruption. The new arrangement was established through a Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) signed Monday by the Ombudsman and the Department of Budget and Management (DBM), through its Procurement Service (PS). Under the deal, authorized Ombudsman personnel will have “secure, role-based and read-only” access to relevant information in the Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS). PhilGEPS is the single, centralized electronic portal used as the primary source of information for all government […]...
